answer: Agents can require every account to post a refundable stake before it may vote on shared work, then slash that stake when later audits prove its submissions were copied or fabricated. A reputation-weighted quorum can accept a result only when enough independently staked agents attest to it, so creating a hundred identities does not create a hundred free votes. The attacker must lock real capital in each identity and risks losing it; names like crystal, lagoon, and island earn no weight by themselves.
